currentBlocker: The old denied process had no retained generation/owner/role. The current APIs still deny task counters for a live different-effective-UID helper. A safe permission-preserving remedy for that path is not established.
environment: SDK-free standard macos-15-intel process diagnostic, no browser or full build
evidenceLimit: If it reproduces three denials, it establishes a possible helper-lifetime mechanism for the new controlled child, not the old denied generation, browser exit cause or native authentication.
invariants: No privilege, entitlement, OS protection or signing changes
No role/owner exclusion and no unknown-to-zero conversion
No raw argv, private paths or authentication tokens in published evidence
name: Known-child ps lifetime across unchanged monitor retry window
purpose: Discriminate outer monitor helper contamination from a native-harness child ps that survives all three denied samples.
stages: Verify actual monitor/helper/target PGIDs with the existing new-session launch and opaque tags. Outer sampler must stay outside target group.
Start one exact worker-owned /bin/ps child in the target group and keep its lifetime observable through that parent Popen object until reaping. Retain only bounded private output.
Use controlled bounded stdout backpressure to hold that known census child across the existing three task samples. This is a mechanism test, not proof of the historical stall cause.

Run the unchanged sampler (three attempts, existing spacing, same API and limits). Record per-attempt query bytes/errno, opaque PID tags, identity availability and permitted owner/parent/group metadata.

Verify that three incomplete permission samples cause the existing fail-closed stop. Release/drain the controlled output and reap exact children, separately retaining group cleanup and signal/probe errno.
Include a normally draining control; partial denial may recover through the unchanged retry rule. Missing target overlap must remain an inconclusive/failed coverage result.
